extracted.intended_audience: Toastmasters contest chairs, chief judges, voting and tiebreaking judges, timers, counters, and contestants
extracted.subtask_description: Official rulebook and standards for conducting and competing in Toastmasters speech contests (International, Evaluation, Humorous, Table Topics, Tall Tales, Video). Covers eligibility, speech composition/originality, timing, judging, protests, props, recordings, and contest procedures.

rubrics_metrics.name: Recognized contest types
rubrics_metrics.description: Toastmasters International recognizes and supports the following official speech contests: International, Evaluation, Humorous, Table Topics, Tall Tales, and Video (only for members of undistricted clubs, including territorial councils and provisional districts). No other contest types, showcases, etc., can be conducted by districts (including areas and divisions).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Districts must conduct the International Speech Contest; may conduct up to three additional English contests and up to four non-English contests per year (non-English contests must not continue beyond district level and may use International rules).

rubrics_metrics.name: Contest progression/selection sequence
rubrics_metrics.description: Contests must originate at the club level and proceed through the area, division, and district levels, respectively; only contests following this progression are permitted at the area, division, and district levels.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rules for run-offs in large districts, replacement of unavailable winners by highest-placed available contestant, options to allow two contestants to advance where few clubs/areas/divisions exist, and requirement that decisions about allowing two contestants advance be made and communicated before contest cycle begins.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contest fee prohibition for contestants and clubs
rubrics_metrics.description: Contestants may never be charged a fee to compete in a contest, and clubs may never be charged a fee to send a contestant to a contest.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Individual admission fees to audience attendees and contest officials may be charged but not to contestants; contest entry fees (if any) must be waived for contestants.

rubrics_metrics.name: Eligibility to compete (general)
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible to compete in any official Toastmasters speech contest, a member must be a paid member of a club in the area, division, and district in which he or she is competing; the club must be in good standing; new, dual, or reinstated members must have dues and membership application current with World Headquarters.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Each contestant must be physically present to compete beyond the club level (no remote participation except specified exceptions). A contestant must maintain eligibility at all levels; if found ineligible at any prior level, disqualification is required even if corrected later.

rubrics_metrics.name: International contest additional eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: To be eligible to compete in the International Speech Contest, a member must have completed six speech projects in the Competent Communication manual or earned certificates of completion in Levels 1 and 2 of any path in the Toastmasters Pathways learning experience.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Exceptions: charter member of a club chartered less than one year before the club contest may compete without this requirement provided the club officially chartered before the area contest.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ineligible persons to compete
rubrics_metrics.description: Specific categories of members are ineligible to compete in any Toastmasters speech contest: members serving as voting or tiebreaking judges beyond the club level for a contest type they are competing in, incumbent international officers and directors, region advisors or applicants, specified district officers whose terms expire June 30, international officer and director candidates, immediate past district directors, district officers or candidates campaigning for upcoming elected positions, presenters of education sessions, contest chairs, contest Toastmasters, chief judges and event committee chairs for the event at which the contest is held.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contest chairs, chief judges, voting and tiebreaking judges, timers, counters, sergeants at arms, and test speakers may not compete in the contest at which they are serving; winners of certain contests (World Championship, Video Speech Contest) have additional ineligibility rules.

rubrics_metrics.name: Judges, chief judge, and tiebreaking judge eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: To be a chief judge, voting judge, or tiebreaking judge, at a club contest be a paid member; at area/division/district contests be a paid member for minimum six months and have completed six Competent Communication projects or Levels 1–2 of Pathways; be physically present. For Region Quarterfinals/Semifinals/World Championship additional minimums apply (paid member for six months, Advanced Toastmaster Bronze or Advanced Communicator Bronze or at least one Pathways path completed, prior judging experience).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All voting judges and the tiebreaking judge must sign Judge’s Certification of Eligibility and Code of Ethics and the tiebreaking judge's identity is secret and does not attend the judges' briefing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speech subject selection
rubrics_metrics.description: The subject of all International, Humorous, and Tall Tales contest speeches must be selected by the contestant. The subject of Table Topics must be determined by the contest chair. Evaluation contest subjects are limited to oral evaluations of the test speaker’s speech.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Contestants must create their own speeches, and each must be substantially original.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality and permitted quoting
rubrics_metrics.description: Contestants must create their own speeches, and each must be substantially original. Twenty-five percent or less of the speech may be devoted to quoting, paraphrasing, or referencing another person’s content. Any quoted, paraphrased, or referenced content must be so identified during the speech presentation.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before all contests, every contestant must certify in writing to the chief judge that the content of their speech is or will be substantially original by using the Speaker’s Certification of Eligibility and Originality.

rubrics_metrics.name: Speaking area and equipment access
rubrics_metrics.description: All contestants will speak from the same platform or area designated by the contest chair. A lectern/podium will be available (optional). If amplification is necessary, a lectern/podium fixed-mounted microphone and a portable microphone must be made available.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All equipment must be available for contestants to practice with prior to the contest. Contestants are responsible for arranging their preferred setup in a quiet manner before being introduced.

rubrics_metrics.name: Number and composition of officials and judges per level
rubrics_metrics.description: Specified minimum numbers and composition of voting judges and officials are required at each contest level (club, area, division, district, region quarterfinal, semifinal, World Championship). Voting judges must not be members of any club in which a contestant is a member at higher levels; voting judges remain anonymous when practical.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Examples: club—at least five voting judges; area—equal number from each club or minimum five; division—equal from each area or minimum seven; district—equal from each division or minimum seven; region quarterfinals—minimum nine voting judges and one tiebreaking judge; World Championship—one voting judge per region plus qualifying and other judges as specified.

rubrics_metrics.name: Contestant briefings and speaking order
rubrics_metrics.description: Before the contest, contestants are briefed on the rules by the contest chair. Contestants will draw for their speaking position with the contest chair. If absent from briefing, the alternate may attend in place of the primary; late arrivals have limited accommodation rules.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: If primary contestant not present when person conducting contest is introduced, primary is disqualified; if arriving after briefing but before introduction, may compete if they report to chair, have paperwork, and waive briefing.

rubrics_metrics.name: Introductions format
rubrics_metrics.description: For the International, Humorous, and Tall Tales contests, introduce each contestant by announcing the contestant’s name, speech title, speech title, and contestant’s name. For Table Topics: contestant’s name, topic, topic, contestant’s name. For Evaluation: introduce contestant by announcing the contestant’s name twice.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Do not make preliminary remarks about any speaker or subject, nor mention the speaker’s club or residence during introductions.

rubrics_metrics.name: Ballot completion and confidentiality
rubrics_metrics.description: Voting judges must complete ballots by entering their choices for first, second, and third place and sign and print their names. Ballots and bottom portions are handled per procedure; all ballots, Counter’s Tally Sheets, and Time Record Sheets are confidential and given to the chief judge for disposal.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Ballot counters tabulate using Counter’s Tally Sheet: 3 points for first, 2 for second, 1 for third; tied totals resolved by consulting tiebreaking judge's ballot; chief judge keeps ballots until winners announced then destroys ballots, time record, and tally sheet.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring and tie-breaking
rubrics_metrics.description: On the Counter’s Tally Sheet each contestant receives points for being ranked first (3), second (2), or third (1) on a voting judge’s ballot. Once totals are entered contestants are ranked; in the event of a tie the chief judge will consult the tiebreaking judge’s ballot.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The tied contestant who received the highest ranking on the tiebreaking judge’s ballot gains the contested place; other tied contestants ranked behind accordingly.

rubrics_metrics.name: Announcement of winners
rubrics_metrics.description: After the conclusion of the contestant interviews, the contest chair announces the winners of the contest in reverse order.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In contests with three or more participants, announce third, second, and first. With less than three participants, announce second (if applicable) and first. Announcement final unless announced incorrectly; chief judge/counters/timers may interrupt to correct errors.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing—timers and devices
rubrics_metrics.description: Two timers are appointed: one with a stopwatch and one with a signaling device that displays green, yellow, and red. Signaling device must be in full view of each contestant; the stopwatch timer maintains written record of elapsed time.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Timers must provide warning signals clearly visible to speakers but not obvious to the audience; special accommodations for visually impaired contestants allowed.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing—when timing begins
rubrics_metrics.description: Timing will begin with the contestant’s first definite verbal or nonverbal communication with the audience. This usually will be the first word uttered, but includes other communication such as sound effects or a staged act by another person.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Speaker should begin speaking within a short time after arriving at the speaking area and not delay contest unnecessarily.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timing windows and disqualification thresholds (contest-specific)
rubrics_metrics.description: All speeches must conform to timing guidelines. International and Humorous: 5–7 minutes (disqualified if <4:30 or >7:30). Table Topics: 1–2 minutes (disqualified if <1:00 or >2:30). Evaluation: 2–3 minutes (disqualified if <1:30 or >3:30). Tall Tales: 3–5 minutes (disqualified if <2:30 or >5:00).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specific green/yellow/red signal timings per contest type are defined (e.g., International/Humorous: green at 5m for 1m, yellow at 6m for 1m, red at 7m until conclusion). No signal for overtime period; in event of technical failure speaker allowed 30 seconds extra before disqualification; prior to announcing results chair must announce if time disqualifications occurred (but not name contestants).

rubrics_metrics.name: Warning signals timing (green/yellow/red)
rubrics_metrics.description: For each contest type the exact times for green, yellow, and red signals are specified (e.g., International/Humorous: green at 5:00 remain 1:00; yellow at 6:00 remain 1:00; red at 7:00 until conclusion). Table lists timings for Evaluation, Table Topics, Tall Tales similarly.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: In all contests no signal can be given for the overtime period; visually impaired contestants may request alternate signals; timers must ensure signals are visible but discreet to audience.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protests—scope and procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Protests are limited to eligibility and originality and must only be lodged by voting judges and contestants. Any protest must be lodged with the chief judge and/or contest chair prior to the announcement of the winner and alternate(s). The chief judge, contest chair, voting judges and contestants must not consider protests from audience members.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Before a contestant can be disqualified on originality, the contestant must be given opportunity to respond to voting judges; a majority of voting judges must concur to disqualify for originality. The contest chair can disqualify on eligibility. All decisions of voting and qualifying judges are final.

rubrics_metrics.name: Use of props and electronic devices
rubrics_metrics.description: Contestants who plan to use props (including any electronic devices) must notify the contest chair prior to the contest. Contestants must abide by venue restrictions on props.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: All props must be set up during the minute of silence prior to the speech and removed in the minute of silence following the speech. Contestants may enlist help but contest officials are not responsible; contestants must demonstrate props can be set up/removed in allotted times or props cannot be used.

rubrics_metrics.name: No digital/other devices for unfair advantage
rubrics_metrics.description: Contestants must not use digital or other devices during the contest to gain an unfair advantage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Specifically called out in Table Topics and Evaluation contest sections; devices not allowed during preparation in Evaluation and during Table Topics speeches.

rubrics_metrics.name: International Speech Contest—language and recording rules
rubrics_metrics.description: The International Speech Contest must only be conducted in English. District-level contest videos submitted to World Headquarters for region quarterfinal judging must meet audio, camera, lighting, and video recording requirements (audio clear, HD single-camera on tripod, entire speaking area visible, monitored by operator, no zooming; lighting fully lit and facial expressions visible; recording must contain introduction and entire winning speech; no editing).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: District must submit Notification of District Winner, Region Quarterfinal Video Release form, and video in the requested format. Video entries that are edited or do not meet requirements will be rejected.

rubrics_metrics.name: World Championship—new speech requirement
rubrics_metrics.description: Every participant in the World Championship of Public Speaking must present an entirely new and different speech than the one presented during that year's semifinal speech contest or any previous year's semifinal and final-round speech contests.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Winners must prepare and deliver outlines of their semifinal-winning speech to World Headquarters for qualifying judges; qualifying judges indicate whether the World Championship speech is entirely new and different; if three of five qualifying judges mark Disqualified for a speaker, that speaker is disqualified (no protest allowed).

rubrics_metrics.name: Evaluation Contest—test speech and preparation
rubrics_metrics.description: At the beginning a five- to seven-minute test speech is presented (must be contest-type, Competent Communication assignment, or Pathways project). Contestants have five minutes to prepare their evaluation after leaving the room; preparatory notes must use the Evaluation Contestant Notes sheet; contestants must not use digital devices to gain an unfair advantage.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Recommended test speaker not be member of same club as any contestant; manual/project objectives must not be disclosed; notes are collected/returned per procedure; introduce each contestant by name twice.

rubrics_metrics.name: Humorous Speech contest—subject, content, and form
rubrics_metrics.description: The subject for the Humorous speech must be selected by the contestant. The speaker must avoid potentially objectionable language, anecdotes, and material. The speech must be thematic in nature (opening, body, and close), not a monologue (series of one-liners).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Humor should be appropriate and thematically structured; avoid objectionable material that could lead to protest or disqualification.

rubrics_metrics.name: Table Topics contest—topic qualities and procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: All contestants must receive the same topic of a general nature selected by the contest chair. The topic must be of reasonable length, must not require detailed knowledge, and must lead to an opinion or conclusion. Contestants receive no advance knowledge; must not use digital devices; contestants except the first must leave the room until their turn.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Introduce each contestant by name, topic, topic, name; next speaker invited in after preceding speaker completes response.

rubrics_metrics.name: Tall Tales contest—subject and permitted aids
rubrics_metrics.description: The Tall Tales speech must be of a highly exaggerated, improbable nature and have a theme or plot. Humor and props may be used to support or illustrate the speech.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Props allowed but must follow general props rules (notify chair, set up/remove in minute of silence, abide venue restrictions).

rubrics_metrics.name: Video Speech Contest—eligibility and submission rules
rubrics_metrics.description: Members of undistricted clubs may participate; videos must be in English. Clubs conduct a contest and submit a video of the winning speech. Only one speech per club may be submitted. Include entire speech including introduction; edited speeches will not be accepted.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Complete and submit Video Speech Contest Entry Form with live URL; time speech to comply with International timing rules; submit Speaker’s Certification of Eligibility and Originality; deadline/time submission rules apply.

rubrics_metrics.name: Timers' written time records and reporting
rubrics_metrics.description: The timer with the stopwatch maintains and delivers to the chief judge the written record of elapsed time of each speech on the Speech Contest Time Record Sheet and Instructions for Timers.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: On conclusion timers complete the timing record sheet and place in provided envelope and hand to chief judge; chief judge verifies and records timing; timing disqualifications must be announced prior to results (without naming contestants).

rubrics_metrics.name: Judges’ briefing materials and procedure
rubrics_metrics.description: Before the contest, voting judges, counters, and timers are briefed on their duties by the chief judge. Each voting judge receives the appropriate Judge’s Guide and Ballot and must sign Judge’s Certification of Eligibility and Code of Ethics.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chief judge briefs counters on tally sheet use, briefs timers on timing sheet and equipment; instruct judges to sit close to contest area and review judge’s guide and ballot and speaking area.

rubrics_metrics.name: Confidentiality, record keeping and disposal
rubrics_metrics.description: All ballots, Counter’s Tally Sheet Forms, and Time Record Sheets are considered confidential. The chief judge keeps them until after winners announced and then destroys ballots, the time record, and the tally sheet.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Chief judge records winner ranking on Notification of Contest Winner form and submits to next level or World Headquarters as appropriate; maintain list of placements in case winners cannot advance.
